chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who enters Makkah during the year, once, or twice, or four times, what should he do? He (peace be upon him) said: When he enters, let him enter while reciting the Talbiyyah; and when he exits, let him exit while being free from Ihram.

He (peace be upon him) said: And for every month there is an Umrah. So I said, Can it be less? He (peace be upon him) said: For every ten days there is an Umrah. Then he (peace be upon him) said: By your right, I have performed six Umras in this year of mine. I said, Why is that so? He (peace be upon him) said: I was with Muhammad ibn Ibrahim in Al-Ta'if, so every time he entered, I entered with him.

key_terms.مُحِلًّا: Free from Ihram (the state of ritual consecration)
key_terms.مُلَبِّياً: Reciting the Talbiyyah (the ritual declaration during Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for performing Umrah multiple times in a year according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the ruling for frequent visitors to Makkah, establishing that each entry and exit constitutes a separate Umrah requiring distinct Talbiyyah and Ihram states. The Imam’s personal practice of performing six Umras in a year while residing in Al-Ta'if serves as a practical precedent, demonstrating that one does not need to leave the Haram boundaries to reset the ritual state, thereby facilitating greater devotion for those residing nearby.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from yunus, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about a man who enters makkah during the year, once, or twice, or four times, what should he do?’ Heasws said: ‘When he enters, so let him enter exclaiming Talbiyya; and when he exits, so let him exit being free from Ihraam’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And for every month there is an Umra’. So I said, ‘Can it happen to be less?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For every ten days is an Umra’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> tell you the truth. I<sup>asws</sup> have performed in this year of mine<sup>asws</sup>, six Umras’. I said, ‘Why is that so?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> was with Muhammad Bin Ibrahim in Al-Ta’if, so every time he entered Makkah, I<sup>asws</sup> entered it along with him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Isma‘il ibn Marrar from Yunus from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who enters Makkah once, twice, three or four times every year, what should he do? He (the Imam) said, ‘When he enters he must do so saying Talbiyah and when he comes out he must do so after coming out of the state of Ihram.

He (the Imam) said, ‘Every month there is al-‘Umrah.’ I then asked, ‘Can it be less?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, in every ten days there is al-‘Umrah.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘Believe me, this year I performed six al-‘Umrah.’ I then asked, ‘How has that happened?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘I was with Muhammad ibn Ibrahim in Ta’if, so every time he entered (Makkah), I also did so with him.’”
